summary: The legacy course layer is 37 authored guided lessons (6 geometry lessons, 7 prerequisite bridges, 13 assessed foundations, 11 core-practice sequences) placed in all 25 chapters. There are about 17,000 words of original prose, 128 justified derivation steps, 37 misconception checks with 111 per-option feedback rationales, and 74 numerical problems with hints and worked solutions (37 transfers plus 37 changed-calculation variants). Five lessons carry synchronized interactive models: charts, metric, basis, transport and horizon. A shared lesson record format (question, intuition, reasoned steps, formal limits, check, transfer, variant, sources, takeaway) is inventoried as its own asset. The curriculum around them has five parts: a 25-chapter prerequisite DAG, three chapter-level routes, a 30-skill readiness map with a validator, 37 placement records that each give an editorial reason, and 25 chapter guides. Every lesson follows the same template: a motivating question, an intuitive account, numbered steps with a stated reason for each, a formal layer that states limits and scope, a predict-then-feedback check, a changed-data calculation, and a takeaway. Scientific care is exceptionally high. Two independent author cross-reviews found no incorrect results (geometry-review.md, causality-review.md). The capstone and curvature-table numbers are independently re-derived by finite-difference Riemann code (check-physics-calculations.mjs). validateCourse() still passes (re-run 2026-09-12), and I hand-verified every transfer and variant answer. For novices the picture is uneven. The geometry, horizon, orbit and capstone lessons are excellent and reusable almost verbatim. The foundations that try to teach electromagnetism, statistical mechanics and quantum states in three steps supply vocabulary rather than competence. Practice is numeric-only, one variant deep, and cannot check method. Routes are chapter-level and long. Everything is hard-wired to book.md headings and chapter-N.html anchors. It is authored as one-line String.raw JavaScript objects, which makes review painful. No learner study was ever run. Recommendation: port the lesson content and misconception feedback into a schema-validated grbook.ai lesson format keyed to concept IDs. Mine the skill map and placement reasons into the concept DAG. Rebuild routes and diagnostics on that DAG, and rebuild practice as parameterized, method-revealing items that the AI tutor can extend.
lessons_learned: Structural validity is not teachability. Acyclic chapter graphs, valid links and passing browser suites all coexisted with a Chapter 0 lesson that required metrics, intervals and connection coefficients (novice-sequencing-audit-2026-09-09.md). grbook.ai needs a recorded editorial reason for every lesson placement, plus a human first-use read, not just graph checks.

Required preparation must not hide behind optional-looking depth tabs. The legacy fix split lessons into section-start PREPARATION (always visible) and section-end WORKED EXAMPLE (tabbed). Keep that distinction as a first-class field.

Answer position leaks. All 13 original checks had the correct choice at index 0 (review F03). The fix rotates choices by lesson index modulo 3, so correct positions still cycle 0,2,1 through the sorted sequence (verified 2026-09-12), and the source still lists every correct answer first. Use a per-learner shuffle with stable choice IDs.

Numeric-only answer checking cannot tell whether the intended method was used. For example, the coordinate-change transfer can be solved without transforming anything (comprehensive review §9, line 314). Design items whose answer requires the method's intermediate object (a transformed component, a Christoffel symbol), or have the AI tutor grade written steps against a rubric.

Heuristic symbol meanings are dangerous. The inspector called the horizon lesson's dimensionless plotting time 'proper time' (review F01). Symbol identity must be scoped to the lesson or equation in the concept registry, and unresolved symbols should get no tooltip.

Chapter-level prerequisites over-constrain and under-constrain at the same time (review F08). The 'short' black-hole route still requires 22 chapters, and omitted edges cannot be detected. Model prerequisites at concept or skill granularity.

A prerequisite subject cannot be taught in a three-step bridge. The electromagnetism, thermal and quantum foundations give correct but compressed vocabulary (novice audit, 'Remaining teaching review'). Either build a real optional module or state the boundary explicitly.
Progressive enhancement matters for content. Hidden derivation panels disappeared without JavaScript (review F05). Lesson text must be readable by default, with interactivity layered on.

Honest evidence language worked and should carry over: 'an independent check is evidence about that example, not mastery'; 'End of route' rather than 'Route complete'; diagnostics 'suggest preparation, not a placement grade'.

Authoring 37 lessons as one-line String.raw objects with LaTeX inside JavaScript made scientific review and diffs hard (review line 503). The variants also live in two different places: a map in practice-variants.mjs and inline variants arrays. Use one schema-validated content file per lesson, one field per line, with a single practice-item format.

Independent physics verification is a pattern worth keeping. Finite-difference Riemann and Einstein-tensor checks against the lesson numbers (check-physics-calculations.mjs) are stronger than testing that a display matches its own formula.

Design docs drifted from reality within a day. course-architecture.md still says 13 bridges and five visual models, and says course.mjs owns the graph. credits.md says both 'three interactive experiments' and 'nine Three.js labs'. Generate counts and ownership statements from the content, or omit them.
Placing a diagnostic item identical to a lesson's own transfer problem spoils the transfer. Diagnostic and assessment items should be distinct.

Chapter bundling, not content, set route length. Chapter 22 packs singularity theorems (which need forms) together with Hawking temperature (which does not), so the black-hole route inherits Chapter 21 and its own prerequisites. In grbook.ai keep unrelated destinations in separate concept clusters so one heavy topic cannot gate another.

Reusing one item for three jobs broke all three. Each foundation skill's check is literally the lesson's transfer prompt, which is also the diagnostic card. Give every concept a distinct pool for diagnostic, in-lesson transfer and later review.
Choice IDs derived from a hash of the option text make stored attempts fragile: any copy-edit to a distractor changes its ID. Author stable IDs explicitly.

Exempting 'basic' skills (calculus, linear algebra) from ordering checks hides exactly the novice gaps the audit found. Validators should treat entry skills as assessed entry requirements, not as always satisfied.

assets.title: One distance, two ways to count it
assets.teaches: A measurement is a number together with a unit. Convert with a ratio equal to one (2 m = 200 cm, 0.5 m/s = 50 cm/s). Squared units square the factor (1 m² = 10,000 cm²). Dimensions are [x]=L, [v]=L/T, [a]=L/T². Dimensional agreement is necessary but not sufficient: x=At² and x=2At² both pass. Transfer: 2 m × 30 cm = 0.60 m². Variant: a 0.5 m square is 2500 cm².
assets.pedagogy: Opening lesson of Chapter 0 (end of §0.1). The hook is 'what changed when the number changed?', followed by three steps (length, rate, area). The misconception check targets comparing numbers across units ('100 times faster'). It was added after reader feedback, once the earlier advanced units lesson was moved out of Chapter 0.

strengths: Genuinely novice-level entry point
Formal layer adds the necessary-but-not-sufficient point about dimensional checks
issues: Very elementary compared with the rest of the course; the check is easy to guess
Does not connect to geometrized units (c=G=1), which is handled separately in dimensions-before-symbols
No visual

reuse.notes: Keep as an optional warm-up card that the tutor can route to when a learner mishandles units. Merge its dimension paragraph with dimensions-before-symbols into one units-and-geometrized-units sequence, and re-key it to concept IDs.

assets.title: A law needs a starting state
assets.teaches: Solve dy/dt=ky with y(0). Build x(t)=x0 cos ωt + (v0/ω) sin ωt from two initial data. Rewrite a second-order equation as a first-order state system (the basis of numerical stepping). Components obeying Ȧ=−ΩB, Ḃ=ΩA keep A²+B² fixed. Initial data differ from boundary data (x(0)=x(π/ω)=0 is not unique). Solutions can blow up in finite time (y=1/(1−t)). Transfer: x(π/4)=3 m. Variant: x(π/3)=−2 m.
assets.pedagogy: Two swings obey the same law but have different histories. A proposed solution must pass two separate checks, substitution and initial data. Step 4 quietly previews the rotating-component structure of parallel transport.

strengths: The state-vector and conserved-norm steps set up numerical evolution and transport
Units kept on ω and kt
issues: The purpose of step 4's rotating system (parallel transport) is never named, so it reads as unmotivated
Check is easy
quality.evidence: novice-sequencing-audit-2026-09-09.md row 'Chapter 0 bridge layers' (dot notation, frequency and oscillator law defined after feedback); transfer answers hand-verified.

reuse.notes: Keep the derivations and the initial-versus-boundary counterexample. Name the payoff of the rotating components ('this is what transport will look like'). Pair with the mechanics/phase-space lab inventoried by the labs group.

assets.title: Motion, stored energy, and pressure work
assets.teaches: d(½mv²)/dt = F·v. With F=−∇U, K+U is constant, and the zero of potential is arbitrary. A piston gives pressure work p dV and dE = δQ − p dV. The unit check 1 Pa = 1 J/m³ says pressure has the dimensions of energy density, which prepares stress-energy and the cosmological fluid equation. Transfer: a 5 m fall gives 10 m/s. Variant: ΔE = −6 J.
assets.pedagogy: Question: 'How can a force exchange energy without making it disappear?' The misconceptions addressed are a held book (force without work), whether insulation blocks work, and whether volume counts as energy.

strengths: Pressure-as-energy-density check is a well-chosen bridge to T^μν and the Friedmann fluid equation
Heat versus stored energy distinguished explicitly
issues: Mechanics, potentials and thermodynamics are compressed into three steps
The heat/internal-energy clarification sits in the formal layer that novices may skip
quality.evidence: comprehensive-course-review-2026-09-09.md §5 table (asked for exactly this bridge); novice audit row 'Chapter 0 bridge layers' (insulation, internal energy, quasistatic defined).

reuse.notes: Split into two cards: energy in mechanics, and pressure work. Keep the piston derivation and the Pa = J/m³ check as the explicit hook into stress-energy.

assets.title: Release two pebbles, not just one
assets.teaches: A freely falling accelerometer reads zero, yet neighboring free-fall paths still separate. With g(z) = −g0 + κz, the separation obeys ξ̈ = κξ. An accelerating coordinate change removes the common acceleration but not the difference. For small |κ|t², Δξ/ξ0 ≈ κt²/2, with the next correction at fourth order. One accelerometer reading cannot tell rocket from gravity. Transfer: 0.03 m. Variant: −0.01 m.
assets.pedagogy: A Newtonian calibration that is labelled as such. It separates 'reading at one event' from 'comparison between neighboring histories', which is the central move of the whole course, and states the local limit quantitatively.
assets.physics_model: Newtonian 1D linear field g(z) = −g0 + κz with ξ̈ = κξ. The lesson states only the short-time expansion ξ0(1 + κt²/2 + O(t⁴)); the closed form ξ0 cosh(√κ t) for κ > 0 (cos for κ < 0) is the reviewer's, not in the source.

strengths: Correct, well-scoped core GR motivation
Makes 'local' a controlled limit with a stated small parameter
Matches the Chapter 1 guide takeaway and check
issues: One-dimensional only; no in-lesson visual even though the free-fall Earth grid and tidal scenes exist
The distractor 'one accelerometer is secretly wrong' is weak
quality.evidence: content/guides.json chapter 1 check/answer; novice audit (§1.1 rebuilt around a spring scale and two test bodies); numbers hand-verified.

reuse.notes: Keep the text. Embed a two-pebble drop interactive (separation versus time, with an accelerating-frame toggle), or link the tidal lab. Replace the weak distractor with 'they separate only because of air resistance'.

assets.title: Change the coordinates. Keep the measurement.
assets.teaches: A sensor moves through the field f=3x−y. Under the nonlinear change u=x, v=y+x², the tangent transforms with J (V'=JV) and the covector with J⁻¹ (ω'=ωJ⁻¹), so df(V)=7 in both charts. Storing covectors as columns explains the inverse transpose. The map is nonlinear, but its action on each tangent space is linear. Transfer: −1. Variant (negative coordinate): 3.
assets.pedagogy: The same measured rate is computed twice, and the compensation is shown explicitly. The misconception check has a classmate transform covector components with J. All quantities are dimensionless, so adding x² to y is legitimate.

strengths: Called 'especially good' by the comprehensive review
Exact algebraic proof plus a worked numeric instance; numerically checked at 25 positions
issues: The transfer can be answered by direct Cartesian computation, so the checker cannot see whether the transformation was done
No in-lesson visual (the covector level-plane scene lives elsewhere)

reuse.notes: Carry the prose, steps and feedback verbatim; only re-key prerequisites to concept IDs. Change the transfer to ask for a new-chart covector component (for example ∂f'/∂u) so that the method is assessed. Link to the covector level-plane lab.

assets.title: Build a boost from exponentials
assets.teaches: Define cosh and sinh from exponentials and verify cosh²−sinh²=1. β=tanh η, γ=cosh η, γβ=sinh η. The boost matrix in rapidity form preserves −(ct)²+x². The inverses artanh and arsinh (with d/dy arsinh y = 1/√(1+y²)) are needed later for a light-delay integral. Collinear rapidities add, giving (β1+β2)/(1+β1β2). Noncollinear boosts include a rotation. Transfer: e^η=2 gives 3/5. Variant: 15/17.
assets.pedagogy: Circle-versus-hyperbola analogy; functions are built from definitions rather than recalled. Placed after the interval (§3.3) following the novice audit.

strengths: Self-contained construction
Explicit warning that boosts in different directions do not commute
issues: No Minkowski-diagram hyperbola visual, where one would help most
The addition formula is asserted in the formal layer rather than derived
The arsinh step is a forward reference whose use is not named
quality.evidence: novice-sequencing-audit-2026-09-09.md row 'Rapidity bridge' (moved after §3.3); comprehensive review chapter 5/16 rows requested the hyperbolic-function bridge.

reuse.notes: Keep. Add an interactive invariant hyperbola with a rapidity slider, and show that composing two boosts adds the parameters. Derive the addition formula in a step rather than in the formal layer.

assets.title: Chase a photon without slowing it down
assets.teaches: A photon's energy as measured by an observer is E_obs = −p·u. For a chasing observer, E_obs/E = γ(1−β) = √((1−β)/(1+β)). The transformed momentum stays null, so the speed is still c. The general factor γ(1−β cos θ) and the aberration formula follow, and these local formulas hold in orthonormal frames in curved spacetime. Transfer: β=3/5 gives 1/2. Variant: approaching at β=−4/5 gives 3.
assets.pedagogy: Resolves the 'same speed, different energy' puzzle with the operational contraction that later underlies gravitational and cosmological redshift.

strengths: Establishes E = −p·u as the reusable definition of measured energy
issues: Short; aberration only stated
Negative β for an approaching observer may confuse novices
No visual
quality.evidence: comprehensive review chapter 3 row (asked for a relativistic Doppler calculation); answers hand-verified.

reuse.notes: Keep as the canonical 'energy is a contraction' lesson and reuse it explicitly in gravitational redshift and cosmological redshift lessons. Replace signed β with 'toward/away' wording plus a small observer-velocity visual.

assets.title: Give one sphere two reliable addresses
assets.teaches: Build north- and south-pole stereographic charts (u,v) = (X,Y)/(1−Z) and (p,q) = (X,Y)/(1+Z), with the inverse map. The transition is (p,q) = (u,v)/(u²+v²), which is its own inverse with determinant −1/(u²+v²)². The Jacobian at (2,0) transforms a tangent (1,2) to (−1/4, 1/2). A chart can fail where the surface is perfectly regular, and a manifold needs no embedding. Transfer: 3/4. Variant: 1/2.
assets.pedagogy: Question: 'What should a map do when the place you want is missing?' Exploding coordinates are presented as a warning about the map, which seeds the later horizon story. The visual keeps both addresses visible for the same point.

Projection from: North pole / South pole

assets.title: Teach a coordinate grid how to measure
assets.teaches: Derive ds² = dr² + r²dθ² from Cartesian differentials. Then g = diag(1, r²), with g_θθ in length² and g_rr dimensionless. At r = 3 m, dr = 0.03 m and dθ = 0.01 give equal lengths. The lesson separates a local tangent norm, a finite chord and a two-leg path, and gives the exact instantaneous speed √(ṙ² + r²θ̇²). Position-dependent components do not prove curvature. Transfer: 5 m/s. Variant: 13 m/s.
assets.pedagogy: Walking between two spokes shows why the same angle means a longer trip farther out. Shrinking the visual's coordinate cell separates an exact local rule from a finite-step approximation.

assets.title: Units belong to coordinates, too
assets.teaches: Every term of ds² has units of length². Relabelling X = ct changes g_tt = −c² into g_XX = −1 while the interval stays the same. [g_ab] = L²/([x^a][x^b]). The Galilean shift y = x − vt produces the mixed coefficient g_ty = v, which has speed units. Setting c = 1 matches time and length units but does not turn angles into lengths. Transfer: g_θθ = 9 m². Variant (q = 2θ): 2.25 m².
assets.pedagogy: Its history is itself a lesson learned. It was first placed at the start of Chapter 0, where it required metrics before they were taught, and was moved to §4.5 while keeping its practice identity.

assets.title: A straight path can have an accelerating label
assets.teaches: Relabelling a straight worldline nonlinearly gives d²x/dσ² + Γ(dx/dσ)(dx/dσ) = (λ''/λ')(dx/dσ), an extra term parallel to the tangent. Only λ = Aσ + B preserves affine form, and λ = √σ gives −1/(2σ). Proper time is affine for timelike geodesics. Null curves need an affine parameter fixed by a physical normalization. Transfer: −1/8. Variant (ln σ): −1/5.
assets.pedagogy: Question: 'Can relabeling points create a nonzero second derivative?' The misconception that every nonzero second derivative is a force is answered by the check.

strengths: Clean chain-rule demonstration that isolates a common confusion
issues: Step 2 jumps to the general-chart equation with Γ without showing the step

No visual, although an affine-parameter figure exists in the figure set

assets.title: An unchanged arrow can have changing components
assets.teaches: A fixed eastward vector expanded in the rotating unit polar frame is cos θ ê_r − sin θ ê_θ. The product rule gives four terms that cancel, and collecting them yields the frame connection (∇_θV)^r̂ = ∂_θV^r̂ − V^θ̂ and (∇_θV)^θ̂ = ∂_θV^θ̂ + V^r̂. Hatted components differ from coordinate components (V^θ = V^θ̂/r). Nonzero connection coefficients can describe a flat plane. Transfer: 1 rad/s. Variant: −2 s⁻¹.
assets.pedagogy: Contrasting the arrow with its address shows that differentiating only the component numbers invents change. The practice pushes on the unit-frame versus coordinate-component factor of r.

interaction.what_updates: Rotating ê_r and ê_θ around the fixed V = (1,0); component values

assets.title: Do the two moves in the other order

Coordinate bases commute, and torsion is T(X,Y) = ∇_XY − ∇_YX − [X,Y]. A noncommuting frame is not by itself curvature or torsion. Transfer: 6. Variant (reversed fields): −3.

assets.title: Carry a direction home—and find it changed
assets.teaches: Tangent projection P = I − nnᵀ. The transport rule P dV/ds = 0 is checked on a great circle. On the octant loop A→N→B→A, the vector goes (0,0,1) → (−1,0,0) → (−1,0,0) → (0,1,0), a right angle equal to area/a² = π/2. A single finite projection is not transport. Norm is preserved, rotation is defined modulo 2π, and the angular excess of a geodesic triangle equals area/a². Transfer: 15°. Variant: 10°.
assets.pedagogy: Question: 'How can an arrow turn if you never turn it?' The local rule comes first, then one verified arc, then the loop. The check asks whether projecting once at the end would do, and why not. It replaced the chapter's older opening animation.

assets.title: Measure curvature without leaving the surface
assets.teaches: C(ρ) = 2πa sin(ρ/a). The ratio C/(2πρ) = 1 − ρ²/(6a²) + O(ρ⁴/a⁴), and K = lim 6/ρ² (1 − C/2πρ) = 1/a². The cylinder is a control: bent but intrinsically flat. Finite circles give only estimates. The general theorem is stated and cited (Kriegl, Thm 11.1), not proved. Transfer: infer a ≈ 2 m from a measured ratio. Variant: a ≈ 5 m.
assets.pedagogy: Could inhabitants discover curvature with a string? The lesson distinguishes the surface radius from the ambient radius and uses an inverse measurement problem as the transfer.

strengths: Second, independent operational curvature measurement alongside holonomy
Transfer is a genuine inverse problem with a self-consistency check
issues: No visual; a string-circle demo on sphere, cylinder and saddle is the obvious companion
Negative curvature (saddle) is not covered

assets.title: A trace loses information you can name
assets.teaches: A six-entry orthonormal curvature table (A..F) with pair symmetries. R_ab = η^cd R_cadb, where the temporal index contributes a sign. The Ricci diagonal is A+B+C, −A+D+E, −B+D+F and −C+E+F. The vacuum counterexample q(−2,1,1,−1,−1,2) has zero Ricci and scalar curvature but Kretschmann 48q², the Schwarzschild pattern. Lorentzian invariants need not be positive. Transfer: R = 24. Variant: R_22 = 8.
assets.pedagogy: Question: 'Can you exhibit nonzero curvature whose entire Ricci tensor vanishes?' A supplied table makes the loss of information under contraction concrete.
